body:
### Summary

When the Python install and bin directories are reached through a symlinked parent directory, `uv python upgrade` treats the existing `python3.X` link in the bin directory as foreign. It warns `Executable already exists at … but is not managed by uv; use uv python install 3.X --force to replace it` and leaves the link alone. This is the default layout on Fedora Atomic desktops (Silverblue, Bazzite, etc.), where `/home` is a symlink to `/var/home`, so every patch upgrade prints the warning. It's probably the cause of https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/15669, which was closed as unreproducible.

Seen with uv 0.13.9 on Linux x86_64. The same steps on a non-symlinked path upgrade the link normally:

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/uvtest/real && ln -s /tmp/uvtest/real /tmp/uvtest/link
export UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR=/tmp/uvtest/link/py UV_PYTHON_BIN_DIR=/tmp/uvtest/link/bin
uv python install 3.11.17
uv python upgrade 3.11   # warns "not managed by uv"; link not repointed
```

Debugged and drafted with LLM assistance.

### Platform

Linux 7.3.4-ogc8.1.fc45.x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### Version

uv 0.13.9 (Homebrew 2026-11-17 x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)

### Python version

Python 3.14.10
title: `uv python upgrade` reports its own bin link as "not managed by uv" when the install path traverses a symlink
